subject: sociology
title: Education Exam Stretch
welcome_lead: Sharpen exam answers with paired perspectives, comparing the functionalist view of schools with Marxist and feminist critiques.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology exam stretch on education, comparing functionalist, Marxist and feminist views.
final_note: Top answers state a view, give evidence, then offer a sociological counter.

walkthroughs.body_html: Functionalists see school as sorting pupils fairly into the jobs they deserve. Marxists call this the myth of meritocracy: results are shaped by class, not ability.

Liberal feminists note girls now outperform boys at GCSE in most subjects but are still steered toward 'feminine' subjects like English. Radical feminists point to lingering male-dominated leadership and sexual harassment in schools.
Open with the named view. Add one supporting study (e.g., Parsons). Add one challenging study (e.g., Bowles & Gintis). End with a clear judgement linked to the question.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between material and cultural deprivation?
options: Material and cultural deprivation are two names for the same poverty.

Material deprivation refers to lack of physical/economic resources (housing, books, food); cultural deprivation refers to lack of skills, values and norms (e.g. parental attitudes to education) that are claimed to support achievement.
Material deprivation is about a lack of clothing; cultural deprivation is about not visiting museums.
Acts are objectively deviant regardless of context.
